title: Twingo I, II and III: what really changes from one generation to another
author: codex-blog-rewrite
excerpt: The Twingo name covers three distinct projects. To observe the model properly, one has to separate what remains from what changes in Renault’s idea of the urban small car.
content:
Behind a stable name, the Twingo has seen three fairly different interpretations. Comparing them shows what Renault keeps, drops or moves when the market and the city change.

First generation: modularity and a new face

The Twingo I presents the most radical project. One-box body, sliding rear bench, central dashboard and a light tone all work together to make the small Renault immediately different.

Its strength lies in that agreement among the details. Shape, space and commercial simplicity all pull in the same direction.

Second generation: more conventional, more equipped

In 2007, the Twingo II enters a more conventional frame. It gains equipment and definition but loses part of the spatial boldness of the first model, especially the sliding rear bench.

The result still has qualities. It fits a denser and more standardised city-car market, yet it shifts the identity carried by the name.

Third generation: rear engine, city use and the electric turn

The Twingo III surprises in another way, with its rear-engine layout born from the Daimler partnership. It regains a real urban singularity through turning circle and compact usefulness.

The later electric version extends that method of the small city car through a different economy of use. The Twingo name continues, even if each generation speaks a different language.
